items.title: Phoebe Jacobs and Jackie Harris interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 21, 2006
items.q: The interviewee does not speak about Kidd Jordan. The interviewer mentions Kidd Jordan as a teacher of Donald Harrison and head of a jazz studies program at SUNO, but the interviewee only responds to the interviewer's narrative without adding personal interaction or specific knowledge of Kidd Jordan

ctx.x: Do you know that Wynton Marsalis is going to be doing three days of a salute to the Hot Five and the Hot Seven at Jazz at Lincoln Center in September of this year? And we succeeded in getting him to have his department market some of the tickets that can be sold for ten dollars to school children so that it isn’t prohibitive for them to come into the Jazz at Lincoln Center, which is quite an expensive ticket.

I think I was under a misconception about New Orleans and kind of what goes on there musically. And I don’t think I’m alone. And that is it occurred to me when I put on a recent CD by Kidd Jordan and the music he was playing was like something John Coltrane had not thought of. And so I realized that I didn’t really know what was coming out of that city.

Well let me start by saying the creative music community is clearly not as large as straight ahead or traditional jazz is. But New Orleans jazz covers every facet of jazz music which we have heard. And artists, young artists, as they develop for the most part, they really go through those different phases of jazz — playing jazz music until they reach the one that they are most comfortable with and the one that they decide that they want to make a career and play. But then too if you look at Nicholas Payton, so…
